newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: McCreevy aims for best possible EU funding package.
newsitem.headline: McCreevy aims for best possible EU funding package.

text.p: Irish finance minister Charlie McCreevy said on Monday that the Irish government's objective would be to ensure that it gets the best available package for Ireland in the next EU funding round.

"The Irish government position will be to try and maximise the amount of funds which we will be entitled to and to try and ensure that this administration is able to secure the maximum amount of funds legally possible to us," he told Irish state radio.
The state broadcaster reported on Friday that EU Commission President Jacques Santer would recommend a reduction in grants and aid to Ireland in an address to the European Parliament on July 16.
The address is expected to cover a reform of EU structural funds, a key component in Ireland's booming economy, and the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP).
The report said Santer's proposals would be linked to the eventual enlargement of the bloc to include former Communist states.
McCreevy declined to outline his negotiating position ahead of Santer's speech.

"There is little point before the Commission package is unveiled next week of starting to negotiate at this point in time. There will be a lot of negotiations between now and the final shape of the negotiations."
But he said that it would be very unwise of any Irish government to hold a referendum on enlargement without putting all the parts in place.

"Before the question of enlargement could be put to the Irish people, any Irish administration would have to be in a position to spell out to the Irish people what the funding proposals would be for the next round, what the future enlargement of the community means vis-a-vis the funding proposals and that is the most sensitive way to approach this particular matter," he said.
